clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of productive cough, fever, night sweats, myalgias, anorexia, and weight loss. Initial chest X-ray showed a large right upper lobe cavitary lesion. Chest CT revealed a 9 × 10 × 14 cm necrotic cavitary lesion with mediastinal lymphadenopathy and vascular compression. Physical examination was unremarkable with no palpable lymphadenopathy. A core needle biopsy was performed and histopathology confirmed classic Hodgkin lymphoma of mixed cellularity type, showing Reed–Sternberg cells and positive immunohistochemical stains for CD15, CD30, and PAX-5.
